result:
I'm staging this as a new project, since nothing works end to end yet. There's no spec with numbered requirements to compare against. Your brief (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`) is the source of the outcomes below. The three research reports are background: they supply facts and costs, and anything only they state is marked as such. Parts A and B of the brief are already delivered by those reports, so the outcomes come from Part C.

One caveat on the costs: I've read only the opening 3,000 characters and headings of each report. The data inventory (ChatGPT report §3.3) and gap sections are unread, so most cost notes below are rough or left for the core stage to measure.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision series for each of the four stages (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark wedge-back), total nonfarm, SA and NSA, from archived vintages | Data volume small (hundreds of monthly rows × a few vintages); the real cost is finding and checking vintage coverage, which only a probe can tell. FRED/ALFRED API limit is 120 requests/min, so it's not a constraint |
| O2 | How the size of revisions (dispersion and tails, not mean) changed over time at each stage, with 2003 and 2020–22 marked as breaks | Cheap once O1 exists; descriptive |
| O3 | Split of the one- and two-month SA revisions into a sample part and a seasonal-factor part, using joint NSA/SA vintages | Needs NSA and SA vintages lined up month by month; ChatGPT report says no published long-run version exists. Fit cost measured by the core stage |
| O4 | Effect of collection interval and first-closing rate on the scale of the one-month revision | Collection days can be computed from release calendars. Closing rates are published, but their history is unread in the reports (Claude report cites 60.4% in 2024). Measured by the core stage |
| O5 | Latent-truth state-space model separating news from noise across the four stages, with the benchmark as an irregular higher-precision observation and wedge-back as its observation operator | NUTS on ~500 months × 4 stages; runtime unknown until run, measured by the core stage |
| O6 | Driver effects partially pooled across NAICS supersectors | Needs supersector vintages (≈11× the O1 data); coverage before 2003 is uncertain |
| O7 | Effect of slow-moving capacity covariates (real appropriations, staffing/FTE, sample size) on revision scale, with honest shrinkage and a statement of what isn't identified | The covariates must be hand-built from budget justifications and FedScope, roughly 40 fiscal years. That is mainly your time, likely days, not compute |
| O8 | Party of the appropriating chambers as a descriptive grouping only | Trivial once O7's annual table exists |
| O9 | Validation against a constant-variance baseline: posterior predictive checks on dispersion, LOO/PSIS, pseudo-real-time | Multiplies fit cost by the number of real-time refits; measured once a model has run |

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Revision record (O1, O2): known progression.** You can likely name its stages: total nonfarm first, then benchmark and wedge-back, then supersectors. Every other track consumes O1.
- **B — Seasonal vs. sample (O3): research.** Split from C because the decomposition holds without any driver answer.
- **C — Collection interval (O4, plus O5 and O9 as its modelling frame): research.** Its effect is identified off within-year calendar variation.
- **D — Operational capacity (O7, O8): research.** Split from C because O4's answer holds without O7's. Joining them would make the collection-interval result wait on the hand-built annual covariates and their identification problems.
- **O6 (supersector pooling)** can be a later item in C or D, or its own track. Your call.

The brief asks for one joint model of all drivers. Under this split, that model becomes where C and D meet later, not something you need before getting a first answer.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- Bayesian state-space framing, with covariates entering the log-scale of a Student-t measurement density.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ, and Polars for the vintage panel.

## Name

`ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

## Probe (optional)

To firm up O1's cost, I can pull the ALFRED vintage list for PAYEMS (total nonfarm payrolls) and one supersector series. That would show how far back first/second/third prints go. I'll only run it if you say yes.

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (especially whether A is a known progression), where O6 goes, and the name.
